Fact.Name: Virginia standard deduction, Filing Status 1 and 3
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(1)(b): $8,500 for taxable years beginning 2024-01-01 and before 2025-01-01 (single; married filing separately takes one-half of the married amount, also $8,500). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 11.

Fact.Name: Virginia standard deduction, Filing Status 2
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(1)(b): $17,000 for married persons filing jointly, taxable year 2024. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 11.

Fact.Name: Virginia personal exemption
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2)(a): $930 for each personal exemption allowable federally. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions Section A.

Fact.Name: Virginia additional exemption, 65 or older or blind
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2)(b): $800 for a taxpayer who is aged or blind under IRC § 63(f). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions Section B: 65 or older on or before January 1, 2025.

Fact.Name: Virginia age deduction, maximum
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5): $12,000 for each qualifying person. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 4.

Fact.Name: Virginia age deduction, last birth date for the full amount
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(a): born on or before January 1, 1939, the full $12,000 regardless of income. A statutory date, kept with the figures so the file holds no date literal outside this block.

Fact.Name: Virginia age deduction income threshold, single
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): the $12,000 is reduced $1 for each $1 of adjusted federal adjusted gross income over $50,000 for single taxpayers.

Fact.Name: Virginia age deduction income threshold, married
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): $75,000 for married taxpayers, measured on the joint AFAGI of both spouses.

Fact.Name: Virginia filing threshold, single
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-321(A): no tax if Virginia adjusted gross income is less than $11,950 for a single individual (taxable years from 2012). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 9.

Fact.Name: Virginia filing threshold, married
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-321(A): $23,900 for an individual and spouse (one-half for married filing separately; this prototype applies the joint figure to Filing Status 2 only).

Fact.Name: Rate schedule, top of the 2% bracket
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-320: 2% of income not exceeding $3,000 (taxable years from 1990). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Tax Rate Schedule.

Fact.Name: Rate schedule, top of the 3% bracket
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-320: 3% of income over $3,000 to $5,000.

Fact.Name: Rate schedule, top of the 5% bracket
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-320: 5% of income over $5,000 to $17,000; 5.75% above.

Fact.Name: Rate schedule, tax at $3,000
Fact.Description: The cumulative figure the 2024 Form 760 instructions print: $60 at $3,000 (2% of $3,000).

Fact.Name: Rate schedule, tax at $5,000
Rate schedule, tax at $17,000
Rate schedule, first rate
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-320: 2% on income not exceeding $3,000.

Fact.Name: Rate schedule, second rate
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-320: 3% on income over $3,000 to $5,000.

Fact.Name: Rate schedule, third rate
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-320: 5% on income over $5,000 to $17,000.

Fact.Name: Rate schedule, top rate
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-320: 5.75% on income over $17,000.

Fact.Name: Credit for Low-Income Individuals, per exemption
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(1): $300 each for the individual, the spouse and each dependent. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ Line 13.

Fact.Name: Poverty guideline, a family of one
Fact.Description: 2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ Line 11, Poverty Guideline Table: $15,060 for one eligible exemption (the 2024 federal poverty guideline).

Fact.Name: Poverty guideline, each additional family member
Fact.Description: 2024 Form 760 instructions, Poverty Guideline Table: $5,380 for each additional person, spouse and dependent exemption ($20,440 for two, $52,720 for eight).

Fact.Name: Virginia Earned Income Credit rate, nonrefundable
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(2): 20% of the federal earned income credit, in place of the Credit for Low-Income Individuals. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ Line 15.

Fact.Name: Refundable Virginia Earned Income Credit rate
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(3)(a): for taxable years 2022 through 2024, 15% of the federal earned income credit, refundable, in place of either nonrefundable credit (20% from 2025, subdivision 3 b). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ Line 16b.

Fact.Name: Military basic pay subtraction, maximum
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(15): up to $15,000 of military basic pay, reduced $1 for each $1 of basic pay over $15,000, so nothing at $30,000 or more. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ subtraction code 38.

Fact.Name: Military benefits subtraction, maximum
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(18)(c): $30,000 of military benefits for taxable year 2024 ($40,000 from 2025), at any age; (18)(d) defines them as military retirement income, § 134 qualified military benefits, and Survivor Benefit Plan and other military benefits paid to a surviving spouse. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ subtraction code 60.

Fact.Name: Commonwealth Savers deduction cap
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7)(a): "limited to $4,000 per prepaid tuition contract or college savings trust account" per return per taxable year. This prototype treats the contributions as one account; the carryforward of the excess to later years is out of scope.

Fact.Name: Commonwealth Savers, last birth date for the no-cap rule
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7)(b): a contributor who has attained age 70 is not subject to the $4,000 limit. Born on or before December 31, 1954 has attained 70 during tax year 2024.

Fact.Name: Virginia resident
Fact.Description: The filer lived in Virginia for all of the tax year, as answered on the federal residence question (/filerResidenceAndIncomeState, with 'va' added to the federal /scopedStateOptions). Part-year and nonresident returns (Forms 760PY and 763) are out of scope. This fact gates the Virginia screens; it is not an export.

Fact.Name: Virginia Filing Status 2, married filing jointly
Fact.Description: Form 760 Filing Status 2 corresponds to a federal joint return. Federal single and head of household file as Filing Status 1; married filing separately as Status 3. Qualifying surviving spouse is out of scope and treated as Status 1 here.

Fact.Name: This filer is the spouse
Fact.Description: Not the primary filer. The federal return exports each filer's /filers/*/isPrimaryFiler to states; the federal /filers/*/isSecondaryFiler and the /secondaryFiler pointer are not exported, so the spouse is found from the flag a state is handed.

Fact.Name: The spouse on a joint return
Fact.Description: The filer who is not the primary filer: how a state's software finds the spouse in what it is handed. Read only on Filing Status 2; the facts below guard that.

Fact.Name: Spouse 65 or older
Fact.Description: On a joint return, the spouse's federal /age65OrOlder (65 on or before January 1, 2025, the rule Virginia's Section B uses). False on any other filing status. A joint return always carries the spouse's date of birth, so the completeness guard only keeps a return with no spouse facts from going incomplete.

Fact.Name: Spouse blind
Fact.Description: On a joint return, the spouse's federal /isBlind (blind for federal purposes, IRC § 63(f)). False on any other filing status.

Fact.Name: Spouse born on or before January 1, 1939
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(a), for the spouse on a joint return: the full $12,000 age deduction regardless of income. Reads the spouse's exported date of birth.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 1, federal adjusted gross income
Fact.Description: Read from the federal return (/agi, exported to MeF as Form 1040 line 11). Line 2 (additions) is out of scope, so Line 3 equals Line 1.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 5, taxable Social Security benefits
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(3): benefits under Title II of the Social Security Act included in federal AGI are subtracted. Read from the federal return (Form 1040 line 6b).

Fact.Name: Adjusted federal adjusted gross income (AFAGI)
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): federal AGI minus Social Security Title II benefits and other benefits taxable solely under IRC § 86. Used only for the age deduction's income test; on a joint return it is the joint figure. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Age Deduction Worksheet lines 2 to 8 (the conformity addition and subtraction on worksheet lines 3 and 5 are out of scope).

Fact.Name: Primary filer born on or before January 1, 1939
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(a): the full $12,000 age deduction regardless of income. Reads the filer's date of birth, which the federal return exports to states.

Fact.Name: Primary filer qualifies for the income-based age deduction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): born after January 1, 1939, and 65 or older. The federal /age65OrOlder uses the same rule as Virginia's instructions (65 on or before January 1 of the following year), so for tax year 2024 it means born on or before January 1, 1960.

Fact.Name: Spouse qualifies for the income-based age deduction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b), for the spouse on a joint return: born after January 1, 1939, and 65 or older.

Fact.Name: Age deduction income threshold for this return
Age deduction reduction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): $1 for each $1 of AFAGI over the threshold, never below zero. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Age Deduction Worksheet line 11. One figure for the return; on a joint return it applies to each spouse's $12,000.

Fact.Name: Age deduction the primary filer qualifies for
Age deduction the spouse qualifies for
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5), for the spouse on a joint return, with the same rule as the primary filer: $12,000 if born on or before January 1, 1939; otherwise, if 65 or older, $12,000 reduced by the return's income-based reduction; otherwise $0. Assumption, from the Code's text: the deduction is "for individuals", and on a joint return "the taxpayer's adjusted federal adjusted gross income" is the joint AFAGI, so each spouse's $12,000 is reduced by the same excess over $75,000. If Virginia Tax's Age Deduction Worksheet instead reduces the couple's combined $24,000 once, this is the fact to change.

Fact.Name: Age deduction the return qualifies for
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5): the primary filer's deduction plus, on a joint return, the spouse's. Line 4 claims this unless the return claims a low-income credit instead (/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 4 and the Age Deduction Worksheet.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 4, age deduction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(5): a return on which the filer or the spouse claims the age deduction cannot claim the Credit for Low-Income Individuals or either Virginia Earned Income Credit. The age deduction the return qualifies for, or $0 when the return claims one of those credits instead.

Fact.Name: Served in, or received retirement pay from, the U.S. Armed Forces in 2024
Fact.Description: Asked, as the gate to the two military questions. Neither basic pay nor military retirement is identifiable on the forms the federal return exports: a W-2 from the military reports box 1, not basic pay, and the federal 1099-R question "is this from a military retirement plan" is not exported to states.

Fact.Name: On extended active duty for more than 90 consecutive days in 2024
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(15). Asked; primary filer only.

Fact.Name: Military basic pay received in 2024
Fact.Description: Basic pay only, from the filer's Leave and Earnings Statements; not allowances, bonuses or special pays, which W-2 box 1 also includes.

Fact.Name: Military basic pay subtraction the filer qualifies for (Schedule ADJ code 38)
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(15): all basic pay up to $15,000; above that, $15,000 reduced dollar for dollar by the pay over $15,000, so nothing at $30,000 or more. Limited to what federal AGI includes, here W-2 wages. The cap is the household's /wages (exported to MeF): the federal per-filer figures (/primaryFilerWages, /formW2s/*/filer, /formW2s/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler) are not exported to states, so the primary filer's own wages cannot be read here; on a joint return the cap is therefore loose by the spouse's wages. Claimed on Line 7 only if the return does not claim a low-income credit (Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(2)).

Fact.Name: Military basic pay subtraction after the phase-out
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(15): $15,000 reduced $1 for each $1 of basic pay over $15,000, never below zero. Only read when the basic pay is over $15,000.

Fact.Name: Schedule ADJ code 38, military basic pay subtraction, as claimed
Fact.Description: The subtraction the filer qualifies for, or $0 when the return claims a low-income credit instead (Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(2)).

Fact.Name: Received military retirement pay or Survivor Benefit Plan payments in 2024
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(18)(c) and (d). Asked; primary filer only.

Fact.Name: Military benefits received in 2024
Fact.Description: The taxable amount (1099-R box 2a) of military retirement pay, Survivor Benefit Plan payments and other military benefits paid to a surviving spouse.

Fact.Name: Taxable amount on every 1099-R of the return
Fact.Description: The sum of box 2a across the 1099-Rs on the federal return (/form1099Rs/*/taxableAmount, exported to MeF in each 1099-R). Military benefits are retirement income, so a military benefits subtraction cannot exceed this.

Fact.Name: Schedule ADJ code 60, military benefits subtraction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(18)(c): up to $30,000 for taxable year 2024, at any age, and never more than the taxable 1099-R income the federal return reports (the subtraction is of an amount "included therein", in federal AGI). It does not bar the low-income credits (§ 58.1-339.8(D) does not list it).

Fact.Name: Schedule ADJ code 37, unemployment benefits subtraction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.02: unemployment compensation included in federal AGI is subtracted in full (2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ subtraction code 37). Direct File puts each 1099-G's box 1 into AGI net of what was repaid in the year, and exports both figures to states (/form1099Gs/*/amount, /form1099Gs/*/amountPaidBackForBenefitsInTaxYear), so the subtraction is their difference, rounded the way the federal /unemploymentCompensation is. No question is asked.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 7, subtractions from Schedule ADJ
Fact.Description: Schedule ADJ Line 7: unemployment benefits (code 37), military basic pay (code 38) as claimed, and military benefits (code 60). The other Schedule ADJ subtractions are out of scope and taken as $0.

Fact.Name: Subtractions the low-income credits do not affect
Fact.Description: Line 5 (Social Security), and on Line 7 the unemployment and military benefits subtractions. The age deduction and the military basic pay subtraction are the two that a low-income credit replaces.

Fact.Name: Line 8 if the return keeps the age deduction and military basic pay subtraction
Fact.Description: Lines 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 with Line 4 and code 38 as the filers qualify for them. Line 6 (state income tax refund, Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(5)) is out of scope and taken as $0.

Fact.Name: Line 8 if the return claims a low-income credit
Fact.Description: Lines 5 + 7 with no age deduction and no military basic pay subtraction (Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(2) and (5)).

Fact.Name: Line 9 if the return keeps the age deduction and military basic pay subtraction
Fact.Description: Line 1 minus Line 8, with Line 4 and code 38 as the filers qualify for them.

Fact.Name: Line 9 if the return claims a low-income credit
Fact.Description: Line 1 minus Line 8 with no age deduction and no military basic pay subtraction (Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(2) and (5)). This is also the family VAGI of Schedule ADJ Line 10.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 8, total subtractions
Fact.Description: Lines 4 + 5 + 6 + 7, as claimed: the with-credit or the without-credit figure, whichever way the return files, so that Line 9 is always Line 1 minus this.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 9, Virginia adjusted gross income
Fact.Description: Line 3 minus Line 8. Va. Code § 58.1-322 defines Virginia taxable income by reference to federal adjusted gross income with the Chapter 3 modifications.

Fact.Name: Virginia filing threshold for this return
Below the filing threshold, keeping the age deduction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-321(A); 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 9: if Line 9 is less than the amount for your filing status, your Virginia income tax is $0.

Fact.Name: Below the filing threshold, claiming a low-income credit
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-321(A); 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 9: if Line 9 is less than the amount for your filing status, your Virginia income tax is $0.

Fact.Name: Virginia adjusted gross income below the filing threshold
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-321(A); 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 9: if Line 9 is less than the amount for your filing status, your Virginia income tax is $0. The with-credit or the without-credit test, whichever way the return files.

Fact.Name: Standard deduction amount for this filing status
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(1)(b). Federal itemizers must itemize in Virginia (Line 10); that case is out of scope, so every return here takes the standard deduction.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 11, standard deduction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(1)(b): a person who can be claimed as a dependent on another's return takes the deduction only with respect to earned income; 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 11, "Dependent on Another's Return": the smaller of earned income and the standard deduction. Earned income here is W-2 wages (/wages, exported to MeF).

Fact.Name: Exemptions claimed in the You, Spouse and Dependents boxes
Fact.Description: 2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions Section A: yourself, your spouse on a joint return, and the dependents claimed federally, counted from each household member's isClaimedDependent, which the federal return exports to states. (The federal /claimedDependentsCount is not exported, so it is not read.)

Fact.Name: Exemptions claimed in the 65 or older and Blind boxes
Fact.Description: 2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions Section B, four boxes: you 65 or older on or before January 1, 2025 (the federal /age65OrOlder rule), you blind for federal purposes, and on a joint return the same two for your spouse.

Fact.Name: Exemptions, Section A amount
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2)(a): $930 times the You, Spouse and Dependents count.

Fact.Name: Exemptions, Section B amount the filers qualify for
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2)(b): $800 times the 65 or older and Blind count, the spouse's boxes included. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions: these cannot be claimed with a Credit for Low-Income Individuals on Line 23 (Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(4) bars every low-income credit when the filer or the spouse claims one).

Fact.Name: Line 12 if the return keeps the 65 or older and blind exemptions
Form 760 Line 12, exemptions
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2): Section A plus Section B, or Section A alone when the return claims a low-income credit.

Fact.Name: Line 14 if the return keeps the 65 or older and blind exemptions
Line 14 if the return claims a low-income credit
Form 760 Line 14, total deductions
Fact.Description: Lines 10 + 11 + 12 + 13, whichever way the return files. Line 10 (itemized) and the Schedule ADJ deductions other than Commonwealth Savers are out of scope and taken as $0.

Fact.Name: Line 15 if the return keeps the age deduction and exemptions
Fact.Description: Line 9 minus Line 14, not below zero.

Fact.Name: Line 15 if the return claims a low-income credit
Fact.Description: Line 9 minus Line 14, not below zero.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 15, Virginia taxable income
Fact.Description: Line 9 minus Line 14, not below zero.

Fact.Name: Tax from the rate schedule, keeping the age deduction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-320, taxable years from 1990: 2% of income not exceeding $3,000; 3% of income over $3,000 to $5,000; 5% of income over $5,000 to $17,000; 5.75% of income over $17,000. Written as the cumulative schedule the 2024 Form 760 instructions print: $60 at $3,000, $120 at $5,000, $720 at $17,000 (the /vaRateSchedule… figures). Rounded to the dollar.

Fact.Name: Tax from the rate schedule, claiming a low-income credit
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-320, the same schedule as /vaWithoutCreditTaxFromRateSchedule, on the taxable income of a return that claims a low-income credit. Rounded to the dollar.

Fact.Name: Line 16 if the return keeps the age deduction and exemptions
Fact.Description: The tax from the rate schedule, or $0 when Virginia adjusted gross income is below the filing threshold (Va. Code § 58.1-321(A)).

Fact.Name: Line 16 if the return claims a low-income credit
Fact.Description: The tax from the rate schedule, or $0 when Virginia adjusted gross income is below the filing threshold (Va. Code § 58.1-321(A)).

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 16, Virginia income tax
Fact.Description: The tax on whichever way of filing the return claims. Line 17 (the spouse tax adjustment) is out of scope, so Line 18 equals Line 16.

Fact.Name: Not barred from the low-income credits outright
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(1) and the 2024 Schedule ADJ eligibility requirements: no credit for a filer claimed as a dependent on another return. The other bars (the age deduction, the 65 or older and blind exemptions, military basic pay, claimed by the filer or the spouse) are elections, weighed in /vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit. The National Guard and federal and state employee subtractions (codes 28 and 39) are out of scope, as is anything a dependent claims.

Fact.Name: Schedule ADJ Line 11, poverty guideline for the family size
Fact.Description: 2024 Poverty Guideline Table: $15,060 for one, plus $5,380 for each more person. Family size is the You, Spouse and Dependents count (/vaPersonalExemptionCount).

Fact.Name: Family VAGI at or under the poverty guideline
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(1). Family VAGI (Schedule ADJ Line 10) is the return's Virginia AGI with no age deduction or basic pay subtraction; a dependent's own income is not on the federal return, so it is taken as $0 here.

Fact.Name: Schedule ADJ Line 13, Credit for Low-Income Individuals
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(1): $300 times the personal and dependent exemptions (Schedule ADJ Line 12; not the 65 or older or blind ones), if the family qualifies.

Fact.Name: Schedule ADJ Line 14, federal earned income credit
Fact.Description: Read from the federal return (/earnedIncomeCredit, exported to MeF as Form 1040 line 27). $0 for a filer claimed as a dependent.

Fact.Name: Schedule ADJ Line 15, Virginia Earned Income Credit
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(2): 20% of Line 14, rounded to the dollar.

Fact.Name: Schedule ADJ Line 16a, the greater of Line 13 or Line 15
Schedule ADJ Line 16b, Refundable Virginia Earned Income Credit
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(3)(a): 15% of Line 14, rounded to the dollar.

Fact.Name: Line 16a, limited to the tax
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(C): a nonrefundable credit cannot exceed the tax (Line 18, here the tax on the return that claims the credit).

Fact.Name: The refundable credit is worth more than the nonrefundable one
Fact.Description: 2024 Schedule ADJ Line 17: "Choose the credit option that benefits you the most."

Fact.Name: Schedule ADJ Line 17, the credit that benefits the filer most
Fact.Description: The lesser of Line 16a and the tax, or Line 16b, whichever is greater.

Fact.Name: Tax less the credit, if the return claims a low-income credit
Fact.Description: Negative when the refundable credit exceeds the tax.

Fact.Name: The return claims a low-income credit
Fact.Description: The election Form 760 leaves to the filer: the instructions for Line 4 say to "claim the deduction or subtraction that gives you the greatest tax benefit." The return claims a credit when there is one and the tax less the credit is lower than the tax keeping everything Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D) says the filer, the spouse or both would give up: the age deduction of either spouse, the 65 or older and blind exemptions of either spouse, and the military basic pay subtraction. Withholding, payments and use tax are the same either way, so this is the whole comparison.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 23, Credit for Low-Income Individuals or Virginia Earned Income Credit
Fact.Description: Schedule ADJ Line 17 when the return claims it; otherwise $0.

Fact.Name: Line 23 is the Refundable Virginia Earned Income Credit
Line 23 is the Credit for Low-Income Individuals
Fact.Description: Line 16a is Line 13 when Line 13 is at least Line 15.

Fact.Name: Line 23 is the nonrefundable Virginia Earned Income Credit
Claiming the credit gave up the age deduction
Fact.Description: Shown on the summary, so the filer sees what the credit replaced and what it was worth; on a joint return the figure includes the spouse's deduction.

Fact.Name: Claiming the credit gave up the 65 or older or blind exemptions
Fact.Description: Shown on the summary, so the filer sees what the credit replaced and what it was worth; on a joint return the figure includes the spouse's boxes.

Fact.Name: Claiming the credit gave up the military basic pay subtraction
Fact.Description: Shown on the summary, so the filer sees what the credit replaced and what it was worth.

Fact.Name: A credit was available, but keeping the deductions saves more
This W-2's box 15 names Virginia
Fact.Description: Direct File derives each W-2's MeF state code (/formW2s/*/xmlStateCd, the StateAbbreviationCd of the W-2 in the Form 1040 XML a state receives) from the residence answer whenever box 15 is filled in, and knocks a return out when a W-2 is from another state (/flowKnockoutBox15IncomeFromDifferentState); the box 15 answer itself (/formW2s/*/state) is not exported. So on a Virginia resident return the code is "VA" exactly when box 15 is filled in, and that is the test here: a resident return and a state code present. Written as a completeness test rather than a comparison with "VA" because the workbench sandbox stands each federal fact in by type and has no per-form string; the two tests agree on every return this module can see, and the ScalaTest asserts the stricter one.

Fact.Name: This W-2's Virginia income tax withheld
Fact.Description: Box 17 (/formW2s/*/stateWithholding, exported to MeF in each W-2) when box 15 names Virginia; otherwise $0.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 19a, Virginia income tax withheld
Fact.Description: The sum of box 17 across the W-2s on the federal return whose box 15 names Virginia. The employer files the same W-2 with Virginia. Line 19b (the spouse's share on a joint return) is folded in here: which filer a W-2 belongs to (/formW2s/*/filer, /formW2s/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler) is not exported to states, so the split cannot be made from the export; a state would match each W-2's employee TIN (/formW2s/*/usedTin, exported) against the filers' TINs instead. Line 19 (19a + 19b) is unchanged by the split.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 20, estimated payments made for 2024
Fact.Description: Virginia Tax received these and holds the record; a state-run filer would fill this line from its own books. This prototype has no connection to those records, so the line is writable and defaults to $0.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 21, last year's overpayment applied to 2024
Fact.Description: From Virginia Tax's own record of the 2023 return. Writable here, default $0, for the same reason as Line 20.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 22, extension payments
Fact.Description: Payments made with Form 760IP; Virginia Tax holds the record. Writable here, default $0.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Lines 19a to 22, tax withheld and paid
Fact.Description: Withholding plus the payments Virginia Tax holds a record of.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 26, total payments and credits
Fact.Description: Lines 19a to 25. Lines 24 and 25 (credit for tax paid to another state, Schedule CR credits) are out of scope and taken as $0.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 27, tax you owe before use tax
Fact.Description: Line 18 minus Line 26 when positive. Line 17 (the spouse tax adjustment) is out of scope, so Line 18 equals Line 16.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 28, your tax overpayment
Fact.Description: Line 26 minus Line 18 when positive.

Fact.Name: Contributed to a Commonwealth Savers (Virginia529) account in 2024
Fact.Description: Asked, because the plan reports nothing to the IRS. Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7).

Fact.Name: Amount contributed to Commonwealth Savers accounts in 2024
Fact.Description: The total paid or contributed in the year, before the per-account cap.

Fact.Name: Primary filer has attained age 70
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7)(b): a contributor who has attained age 70 is not subject to the $4,000 limit. Born on or before December 31, 1954 for tax year 2024 (/vaCommonwealthSaversAge70BirthDateCutoff). Reads the exported date of birth. The contributions are asked of the primary filer only, so the spouse's age does not enter.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 13 (Schedule ADJ), Commonwealth Savers deduction
Fact.Description: Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7): the contribution, capped at $4,000 unless the filer has attained age 70. The other Schedule ADJ deductions are out of scope.

Fact.Name: Bought something in 2024 without paying Virginia sales tax
Fact.Description: Online, by mail or out of state, where the seller charged no Virginia tax. Form 760 Line 33 (consumer's use tax); no seller reports it, so the filer is asked. The form also has an oval to fill when no use tax is due.

Fact.Name: Total of purchases on which no Virginia sales tax was paid
Fact.Description: 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 33: the instructions offer a lookup table for totals under $1,000 and a worksheet above that; this prototype applies the rate directly.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 33, consumer's use tax
Fact.Description: The untaxed purchases times the rate for the filer's locality (/vaUseTaxRate in the virginiaLocalities module), rounded to the dollar; $0 when the filer had no untaxed purchases.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 35, amount you owe
Fact.Description: Line 27 plus Line 34 when there is tax owed; otherwise Line 34 less the overpayment on Line 28 when that is positive. Line 34 here is the use tax alone: Lines 29 to 32 (overpayment credited to next year, voluntary contributions, penalty and interest) are out of scope.

Fact.Name: Form 760 Line 36, your refund
Fact.Description: Line 28 less Line 34 when positive.

Fact.Name: Everything on the what-is-known screen is right
Fact.Description: Asked after the facts are shown. No sends the filer to the correction screens. Flow control only; not a return value.

Fact.Name: The filer wants to correct something
What can be corrected here
Fact.Description: The three things the prototype lets a filer correct on the Virginia side: the date of birth (a fact the filer stated), a W-2 (a document, corrected as a whole) and a payment Virginia's records show (Lines 20 to 22, the records stand-in). Calculated amounts are never editable.

Fact.Name: What the filer chose to correct
Correcting the date of birth
Correcting a W-2
Correcting a payment Virginia's records show
Fact.Description: Lines 20 to 22 are filled from the records stand-in (js/virginia-records.js) once per identity and never overwritten after that, so a correction made here persists.

Fact.Name: The one box on the sign screen
The declaration box on the sign screen, checked
Fact.Description: A single USWDS checkbox (a multi-enum with one option, the only checkbox the runtime renders) carrying the Form 760 declaration as its label. Required: the sign screen cannot be left until it is checked, and js/virginia-sign.js refuses to send without it.

Fact.Name: The filer signed the declaration and pressed Send to Virginia Tax
Fact.Description: Set to true by the Send button on the sign screen (js/virginia-sign.js) once the declaration box is checked, and back to false when the box is cleared. False until then. Demonstration only: nothing is transmitted; the screen says so when this is true.

Fact.Name: The identity the records stand-in was last applied for
Fact.Description: Last name and date of birth, joined with a bar, as js/virginia-records.js keys the stand-in. The stand-in writes Lines 20 to 22 only when this differs from the identity on the return, so a correction the filer makes to those lines is never overwritten.

Fact.Name: Virginia's records hold a match for this filer
Fact.Description: Set by js/virginia-records.js: true when the stand-in has a record under the filer's last name and date of birth, false when it has none (and Lines 20 to 22 are $0). Incomplete until the stand-in has been consulted.

Fact.Name: The name of the locality the filer's ZIP code lies in
Fact.Description: Written beside /vaLocalityFromAddress by js/virginia-locality.js, from the ZIP table's names. A proper noun, the same in every language.

Fact.Name: The name of the locality the filer chose
Fact.Description: /vaLocality as the filer reads it, for the confirmation callout and the use-tax screen. Proper nouns, the same in every language; one case per option of /vaLocalityOptions.

Fact.Name: The return ends with an amount owed
Fact.Description: Line 35 is positive. Gates the owe row on the summary and the running estimate.

Fact.Name: The return ends with a refund
Fact.Description: Line 36 is positive. Gates the refund row on the summary and the running estimate.

Fact.Name: The return ends even: nothing owed, no refund
The basic pay entered is at or above the amount where the subtraction ends
Fact.Description: For the note under the basic pay question: at $30,000 or more nothing is subtracted (Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(15)).

Fact.Name: The military benefits entered exceed the $30,000 the subtraction covers
The Commonwealth Savers contribution entered exceeds the cap, and the cap applies
Fact.Description: For the note under the contribution question: above $4,000 only the cap is deducted unless the filer has attained age 70 (Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7)).

Fact.Name: The bottom of the rate bracket Line 15 falls in
The tax at the bottom of the bracket Line 15 falls in
The rate on the part of Line 15 above the bracket's bottom
The marginal rate as a number of percent
The marginal rate, printed: 2, 3, 5 or 5.75
Fact.Description: The percent sign is in the sentence that shows this.

Fact.Name: The part of Line 15 above the bracket's bottom
The marginal rate times the part of Line 15 above the bracket's bottom
Fact.Description: Line 16 before rounding is the tax at the bracket's bottom plus this; the schedule's tax-at-top figures are whole dollars, so the rounding falls here.

Fact.Name: Rate schedule rate 1 as a number of percent
Rate schedule rate 1, printed
Fact.Description: For the Line 16 disclosure; the percent sign is in the sentence.

Rate schedule rate 2, printed

Rate schedule rate 3, printed
Fact.Description: For the Line 16 disclosure; the percent sign is in the sentence.

Rate schedule rate 4, printed

Fact.Name: The use tax rate as a number of percent
The use tax rate where the filer lives, printed: 5.3, 6, 6.3 or 7
Fact.Description: The percent sign is in the sentence that shows this.
